speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent, and I see a skin condition on your left dorsal hand. To begin my evaluation, can you describe how long you have had this issue and what it looks like?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Given your age, sun exposure, and outdoor activities, have you noticed any new spots on your left hand, and are they changing in color, size, or shape?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. The presence of a rough, scaly plaque on the dorsal hand in a 65-year-old female with significant sun exposure is highly characteristic of actinic keratosis, which is a precursor to squamous cell carcinoma. While your lack of pain is consistent with this condition, I need to confirm the extent and appearance before finalizing the plan. REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide a close-up clinical photograph of the lesion on your left dorsal hand.
